A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOMP expressivity study and MCN/SMCN architectures. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 8 and Table 1 report original Torus experiments: SMCN distinguishes all 223 pairs, while HOMP distinguishes none.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G report Torus experiments, topology-prediction and molecular-property results, learning curves, and measured runtimes.

M1.justification: V1's SMCN combines PPGN-based PPCN updates with cross-rank SCN updates. V2 retains the cross-rank update as SCL but extends it to equal ranks and explicitly selects subgraph updates instead of the PPGN branch (Section 6, Appendix D). This changes a central computational component and its expressivity/runtime tradeoff; the underlying MCN construction is retained.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only synthetic Torus pairs. V2 retains that coverage and adds cross-diameter prediction on lifted ZINC-12K graphs, second Betti-number prediction using ZINC-FULL, and molecular-property tasks on ZINC-12K, MOLHIV, MOLESOL, and MUTAG. MUTAG appears in Appendix G.3 and Table 3.

E2.justification: V1's empirical comparison is SMCN versus HOMP. V2 adds CIN and custom HOMP comparisons for topology prediction, and reported graph-task comparisons with GCN, GIN, CIN++, CIN + CycleNet, Cellular Transformer, PPGN, PPGN++, and multiple subgraph architectures (Tables 1–3). Runtime comparisons additionally include CIN and GNN-SSWL+. These are reported comparisons, without establishing that every cited baseline was rerun.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial evaluation designs: feature removal, cyclic lifting through length 18, normalized targets, accuracy/MSE evaluation, and parameter budgets for topology prediction. The Betti task uses 5,100 balanced examples with a 60/20/20 split; molecular tasks introduce MAE, ROC-AUC, and RMSE evaluation. The original Torus size bounds and significance-based protocol remain; newly specified Torus settings are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: V2 adds convergence comparisons for both topology-prediction tasks (Figure 15) and a practical scalability study covering dataset construction, training, and inference against CIN and GNN-SSWL+ (Appendix G.4). Section 6 also reports a qualitative PPGN-versus-subgraph component comparison. V1 contains no corresponding empirical convergence or runtime analyses.

E5.justification: V1 reports significance-based Torus separation without multi-seed performance summaries. V2 introduces means and standard deviations over five runs with seeds 1–5, alongside repeated runtime measurements and averaging over ten runs or epochs (Appendix G, Tables 4–5). The Torus significance criterion is retained; the PDFs do not establish an increased run count for that original experiment.

E6.justification: The Torus counts remain 223 versus 0. New results include SMCN's 0.060 ZINC MAE, 81.16 MOLHIV ROC-AUC, and 0.809 MOLESOL RMSE (Table 1), plus 92.76% cross-diameter and 99.61% Betti-number accuracy (Table 2). MUTAG accuracy is 92.5%, slightly below CIN and SUN's 92.7% means (Table 3). Tables 4–5 add runtime results. These are additional outcomes, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V2 removes the HOMP–EHNN propositions and proofs from v1 Section 4.4/Appendix A.4, adds expressivity arguments against graph and topological baselines in Appendix F.3, and revises SMCN proofs to use subgraph updates directly. Definition 3.1 also changes strict rank monotonicity to weak monotonicity and explicitly requires singleton rank zero. Most original topology results survive relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion drop HOMP's comparison with EHNN as a core contribution. They expand the contribution from one Torus benchmark to three topology benchmarks and add claims of improved real-world graph prediction over HOMP and expressive GNNs. The central HOMP blindspot, MCN full-expressivity, and SMCN mitigation claims remain.

C2.justification: The main limitations—superlinear scaling and unresolved general orientability/homology expressivity—remain. V2 adds localized interpretations of reduced variability and faster convergence as more stable learning, and attributes runtime gains to fewer subgraph updates using higher-order information (Appendix G). It also qualifies Cellular Transformer expressivity comparisons and removes the speculation about HOMP/EHNN incomparability.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code/data repository link and extensive implementation information in Appendix G: software, hardware, initialization, marking strategies, block equations, readouts, architecture configurations, and optimization settings. It newly documents the retained Torus experiment's 64 permutations, parameter-matched comparator, 20 epochs, learning rate, and hidden dimension. These details were absent from v1's brief experimental description.

R1.justification: V2 removes the dedicated EHNN positioning and associated hypergraph references, while expanding discussion of methods that inject precomputed topology, including Horn, Chen, Rieck, and Buffelli. Appendix F.3 adds substantive positioning against subgraph GNNs, CIN++, CycleNet, and Cellular Transformer. This changes the comparative research framing beyond adding benchmark citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and methods undergo extensive rewriting and compression. SMCN expressivity becomes Section 6.1, detailed architecture descriptions and many proof sketches move into reorganized appendices, and new background and implementation sections reshape the narrative. SCN/SCL and cross-diameter terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 revises the architecture diagrams, removes the PPCN illustration and EHNN counterexample, and adds boundary, neighborhood, implementation-block, and sequential/parallel diagrams. It introduces learning curves and benchmark/runtime tables, including a color-grouped comparison table. Existing illustrations are redrawn or relocated, while the original Torus table's results are retained in prose.

improvement.justification: V1's empirical support consists only of Torus pair separation. V2 substantially addresses that limitation through topology-learning tasks, molecular-property evaluations, uncertainty reporting, and measured computational costs (Tables 1–5, Appendix G). Detailed implementation and access information also make the work considerably more reproducible. Removing the EHNN analysis reduces theoretical breadth, and scalability limitations remain, but the stronger validation and documentation provide a substantial overall quality gain.
